Job Description

Turn sales strategies into real action and make changes happen. If you enjoy implementing new sales processes and best practices, you should definitely read on!

The role you’ll play

As our Sales Operations Manager, you’ll focus on implementing changes across our Sales organisation and ensuring that new initiatives are adopted in practice. We have new ideas and visions in abundance; however, we need your experience and drive to fulfil their potential and ensure the changes become part of our everyday ways of working.

You’ll work on initiatives that support our Business Development (BD) and Account Management (AM) teams, helping us improve the adoption of sales methodologies, standardise sales presentations, introduce new products and services, and establish a common training baseline.

The team you'll be a part of

You will be part of our Sales Operations team with 3 other colleagues, and part of the wider Sales Excellence Department, which also consists of Solution Sales (expert pre-sales) and Onboarding (expert post-sales). Shared across the three teams is a deep interest for both our industry, best practice sales methodology, and how we can do more with AI.

If you want to make a difference, make it with us by…

• Ensure we keep having transparent and clear sales methodologies, even with a constantly changing environment of new product launches and AI-tools

• Further improve sales performance and sales analytics via. leveraging HubSpot features

• Drive the implementation and adoption of new ways of working – for example an AI-tool for RFP completion, updated sales presentation, or demos of our new products

• Be both inspiring and firm with your colleagues – change can be hard, and we are both supporting and demanding of our colleagues

In one year, you’ll know you were successful if…

• Our sales colleagues clearly know when and how to use which processes and tools to sell

• We can quickly and efficiently launch new products and services

• You are recognised as a sales process expert by your colleagues

Desired experience and competencies

What does it take to work for LanguageWire?

What you'll need to bring

• 3+ years of experience in a similar role in Sales, Commercial management, Consulting or similar

• Demonstrated track record of driving change programs

• Strong analytical mindset to analyse sales performance data and recommend actionable improvements.

• Even stronger emotional intelligence, as change requires convincing both hearts and minds

• A genuine interest in our industry – we believe we need to care about something to sell it

This will make you stand out

• Master’s degree in business, economics, or a related field

• Similar experience in a scale-up environment

• Impressive examples of impact

• Genuine interest for LanguageWire

Your colleagues say you are

• A pro-active, diligent and trustworthy colleague – you will get a lot of freedom to design the change programs.

• An inspiring communicator – we need someone who can also sell the vision of change

• An open, brave, and kind extrovert – you should not be afraid of calling 10 colleagues to hear why they are not (yet) doing the change

Our perks

• Enjoy flat hierarchies, responsibility and freedom, direct feedback, and room to stand up for your own ideas

• Internal development opportunities, ongoing support from your People Partner, and an inclusive and fun company culture

• International company with over 300 employees. Offices in Copenhagen, Aarhus, Stockholm, Varberg, London, Leuven, Lille, Paris, Munich, Hamburg, Sophia Antipolis, Atlanta, Helsinki, Turku and Valencia

• We have a hybrid work model called FlexiWire. We offer weekly flexibility, working three days in the office and two days from home. Together with your team, you can coordinate which days to collaborate in the office.

• We take care of our people and initiate many social get-togethers, from Friday Bars to Summer or Christmas parties. We have fun!

Aarhus

• 18 great colleagues the Aarhus office belonging to different business departments

• A lovely office in the city center with great colleagues and a very friendly and helpful atmosphere

• A wonderful terrace so you can enjoy your lunch outdoors, and it also makes for a great venue for summer parties

• Also, epic quizzes and games at parties, and legendary drinks (we have the best bartenders)

Copenhagen

• 34 great colleagues in the Copenhagen office belonging to different business departments

• Open office space with large windows, bringing a light and chill atmosphere for informal chats with colleagues

• Catered lunches every day

• The comfiest couches you will ever sit on

• Monthly Town Hall events broadcast from the office

• Conveniently located close to multiple public transportation options, with private parking available for those who drive to work

About LanguageWire

At LanguageWire, we want to wire the world together with language. Why? Because we want to help people & businesses simplify communication. We are fueled by the most advanced technology (AI) and our goal is to make customers' lives easier by simplifying their communication with any audience across the globe.

Our values drive our behaviour

We are curious. We are trustworthy. We are caring. We are ambitious.

At LanguageWire, we are curious and intrigued by what we don’t understand. We believe relationships are based on honesty and responsibility, and being trustworthy reinforces an open, humble, and honest way of communicating. We are caring and respect each other personally and professionally. We encourage authentic collaboration, invite feedback and a positive social environment. Our desire to learn, build, and share knowledge is a natural part of our corporate culture.

Working at LanguageWire — why we like it:

“At LanguageWire, we use our years of expert experience and knowledge that we've built up in the language industry to share best practices with our customers. We show that we can be a trusted and caring partner by helping our customers to constantly improve their processes by recommending various solutions. In doing so, we can celebrate their successes together”.

(Anna-Karin, Business Development Director, Varberg)

Yes, to diversity, equity & inclusion

In LanguageWire, we believe diversity in gender, age, background, and culture is essential for our growth. Therefore, we are committed to creating a culture that incorporates diverse perspectives and expertise in our everyday work.

LanguageWire’s recruitment process is designed to be transparent and fair for all candidates. We encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply, and we ensure that candidates are provided with an equal opportunity to demonstrate their competencies and skills.

Want to know more?

We can’t wait to meet you! So, why wait 'til tomorrow? Apply today!

If you want to know more about LanguageWire, we encourage you to visit our website!

The Senior AI Adoption Lead takes ownership of ALK's continuous AI adoption programme, turning enthusiasm into real, safe, everyday value from the AI tools available to ALK employees. This role continues the adoption efforts from 2025 (over 1,000 employees trained in GenAI usage) and 2026 (more tailored training on ALK's AI solutions) and is key to achieving ALK's AI ambition within the Allergy+ strategy.

This role requires genuine enthusiasm for enabling people, facilitating great learning experiences, and driving change. The Senior AI Adoption Lead must work closely with people across all business areas, be proactive, reach out to employees, and drive AI adoption across the entire organization so that the change is permanent and sticks with employees.

This role owns ALK's continuous AI adoption programme, covering general enablement on GenAI, tailored upskilling for all employees, and engagement activities that drive adoption. This includes preparing and hosting AI training (both general-purpose and tool-specific), the training calendar, micro-learning, maintaining AI at ALK intranet site. The role also owns measuring GenAI usage across the organization, providing the data needed to support informed decisions in AI strategy implementation.

This is not an engineering role – the person does not need to build or configure AI solutions. It does, however, require basic understanding of both business and IT, so the Senior AI Adoption Lead can act as an effective bridge between the two. Genuine enthusiasm for new technologies, especially generative AI, is required. Experience with usage of those technologies in daily life and enterprise scenario is vital.

The Senior AI Adoption Lead acts as a proxy between business and IT: translating technical concepts into everyday business language, aligning business demand with IT delivery, triaging common issues, and accelerating adoption before escalation to IT.

This role is based in Denmark, where ALK has its headquarters and the majority of AI users. It also requires occasional business travel to conduct in-person workshops and training.

Major fields of responsibility:

• 
Communicate the need for AI adoption through meetings, newsletters, MS Teams, and Intranet; share success stories, best practices, and enthusiasm for upcoming initiatives.

• 
Foster engagement through targeted workshops for departments and business units, regular manager briefings, tailored communications, and a visible emphasis on the benefits of AI in daily work.

• 
Map use cases and design training courses (e.g. Foundations, Advanced Prompting, Leading with GenAI) and micro-learning, and activate and coordinate a network of AI Champions to extend reach.

• 
Provide accessible, tiered learning resources through the AI community and Learning Hub (Teams channel, SharePoint) — videos, live webinars, in-person workshops, quick-start guides, FAQs, and playbooks.

• 
Support enterprise-AI pilots with onboarding, enablement and value evaluation; collect feedback and resolve common non-technical issues; and maintain a tight feedback loop with IT on platform updates, governance, and support to keep adoption aligned and safe.

• 
Work side by side with the technical teams (programmers, architects, data and platform specialists): take part in solution and roadmap discussions, learn how the solutions work, ask questions from the end-user perspective, challenge and advise on usability, and translate the outcome into layman terms for the business.

• 
Define and measure adoption rates and satisfaction (usage, surveys, focus groups) and report impact to leadership; run iterative cycles to refine training content based on user feedback and business priorities; and recognize high adopters through awards and acknowledgment.

Qualifications:

• 
Minimum 10 years' experience in change management, IT systems adoption, and training management and delivery

• 
Proven facilitation, training and change-management experience

• 
Outstanding communication and stakeholder skills across all levels

• 
Fluent in English.

• 
Hands-on curiosity about generative AI

• 
Practical experience with creation of AI assistants (e.g. custom skills in Anthropic Claude or custom agents in M365 Copilot).

• 
Analytical mindset able to translate adoption data into actionable insights.

• 
Self-driven, organized and creative, comfortable working across business and IT**.**

About Hemab

Hemab is building preventative treatments for serious, underserved bleeding disorders. These are therapies designed to work with the body's own biology and stop bleeds before they start, instead of treating them after they happen. We're patient-first, science-led and clinical-stage - with a pipeline that takes different scientific approaches to different patient needs.

We went public via our 2026 IPO, and we're scaling across two homes: Cambridge, MA, USA, and Copenhagen, Denmark.

The role

As Financial Analyst, you'll own the day-to-day financial planning and analysis (FP&A) across clinical programmes, research and corporate functions. You'll turn financial data and input from colleagues into reliable forecasts, useful insights and clear reporting that helps Hemab make informed decisions.

Working closely with the FP&A Director, you'll take ownership of recurring financial activities while helping build practical ways of working as Hemab grows. Your work will give our teams greater financial clarity and help us make thoughtful decisions about the resources behind our science.

What you'll do

• Own monthly FP&A activities across assigned clinical studies, research projects and functions, keeping forecasts accurate and up to date.

• Partner with functional leads and project teams to understand spending, challenge assumptions and identify financial risks and opportunities early.

• Coordinate quarterly forecasts and contribute to the annual Investment Plan and Long-Range Plan.

• Analyse actuals against forecasts, explain variances and turn financial information into clear, useful insights.

• Prepare management reporting, financial commentary and decision materials for review by the FP&A Director.

• Maintain and improve Power BI reporting, ensuring reliable data and consistent financial information.

• Manage routine financial follow-up with CROs and vendors, including invoice reviews, change orders and financial input to negotiations.

• Build straightforward financial frameworks and reporting practices that help teams work efficiently as Hemab grows.

What you'll bring to Hemab

• Experience in FP&A, forecasting, management reporting and financial business partnering.

• Strong financial analysis skills, with the ability to turn complex information into practical recommendations.

• Advanced Excel skills and hands-on experience with Power BI.

• Experience managing forecasts independently, identifying material changes and knowing when to escalate.

• Ability to work effectively with finance and non-finance colleagues, communicate clearly and challenge assumptions constructively.

• Professional fluency in English.

Nice to have

• Experience in biotech, pharma, clinical development, CROs or another project-driven environment.

• Familiarity with clinical study budgets, vendor financial management or financial planning systems.

• Experience improving financial reporting or building ways of working in a growing organisation.

What to expect, honestly

Hemab is still building a lot of its own structure. Systems here tend to get created as we need them, not handed down in advance. Whoever takes this role will likely build some of their own process instead of inheriting a finished one. We work across two hubs and multiple time zones - bridging that well takes real, deliberate effort. And because we're growing quickly, priorities can shift with less notice than they would at a larger, more established company.

We value people who take ownership, solve problems, ask for help when needed and work without ego. At our size, how you work matters as much as your CV. Good structure should help people move faster and trust the numbers, not slow them down.

Why Hemab

At Hemab, your work ultimately connects back to something simple. People living with serious bleeding disorders get something they've never had before - the chance to prevent a bleed, instead of reacting to one after it happens. You'll be joining at a stage where individual decisions still carry real weight, and where your work can help turn promising science into a preventative treatment that actually reaches patients.

How we treat our people is meant to be an extension of how we think about patients: with care, honesty, and respect. We're still building the consistency to back that up across every hiring process, every time. We'd say that plainly instead of pretending otherwise. If any part of your experience with us falls short of it, tell us.

Hemab builds balanced candidate slates and assesses everyone against a single standard. If you need a reasonable adjustment at any stage of the hiring process, please tell us.

Create high-quality Group reporting, strong internal controls and transparent financial processes across out international organization.

Would you like to help create and further develop the foundation that enables our European finance community to deliver high-quality consolidated reporting for decision makers and our owners on ongoing basis? On behalf of Scanmetals A/S, Leadr Recruitment is looking for a Group Finance Controller who combines strong group reporting and consolidation capabilities with curiosity for ERP, structure, IT tools and hands-on with data in an international environment.

You will work closely with the Group CFO, the executive management team and local finance functions across four countries. You will be the main driver of strengthening reporting, controls and performance reporting including compliance with Danish and International accounting standards.

Your role

You will take on a broad role in Group Finance, working close to the business. You will take the lead in monthly reporting and closing, while also developing the structures, tools and decision support behind the figures. Your work will cover areas such consolidation including eliminations of P&L, balance sheet, cashflow, investments and KPI´s, securing data quality, development of our consolidation platform along with the master data to secure the foundation for high-quality reporting - giving management a more precise basis for taking decisions.

Your key responsibilities:

• Gather and quality-assure monthly group reporting for all subsidiaries across Denmark, Germany, Spain and the UK, including the income statement, balance sheet, cash flow and operational KPIs.

• Handle consolidation entries, intercompany reconciliations and group adjustments.

• Drive and support month-end and year-end closing, coordinate documentation and participate in review meetings with the subsidiaries.

• Ensure consistent, high-quality data and work with IT to further develop reporting in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, Power BI, consolidation system and related tools.

• Contribute to financial budgets, forecasts, cash flow analyses and decision material for the CFO and executive management team.

• Maintain and develop internal controls, accounting processes and compliance across countries and entities.

• Coordinate audit activities and contribute to transfer pricing, tax, VAT, banking matters and the financial aspects of sustainability reporting.

• Drive practical improvements, standardisation and automation across Group Finance.

What you bring:

• A relevant master’s degree in finance, accounting, auditing or a comparable field.

• Experience from audit - preferably from a larger audit firm - combined with solid experience in group accounting or consolidation.

• A sound understanding of Danish and international financial reporting.

• Strong Excel skills and confidence working with ERP and reporting platforms. Experience with Business Central and Power BI is an advantage.

• Fluent English. Danish and/or German is an advantage, but not a requirement.

How you work

You are structured, detail-oriented and dependable, while keeping deadlines and commercial relevance firmly in view. You ask the right questions, are naturally curious, build strong relationships across functions and countries, and take ownership. You thrive in an entrepreneurial business where structures continue to evolve, and the impact of your work quickly becomes visible.

The Mission

Phanofi is a DTU spin-out building the next generation of optical communication infrastructure. We design integrated photonic interconnect chips that reduce power consumption and increase data throughput for AI datacenters, quantum computing, and space applications.

Getting photonic integrated circuits (PICs) out of the lab and into packaged, manufacturable modules is one of the hardest problems in our field, and often the one that decides whether a promising chip becomes a product. As a diverse team of 16, we are at an inflection point, growing our engineering capability to take our photonic interconnect technology from prototype toward scalable, production-ready products.

As Senior Photonics Packaging Engineer, you own that transition. You will work in tight collaboration with our electronic, R&D and photonic engineers and our CTO, with real influence over technical direction as we scale.

Key Responsibilities

You own the packaging of our PICs end to end: turning a functional die into a robust, manufacturable module. In practice that spans the optical interface (fiber attach, alignment and bonding), the electrical interface (from DC and control lines through to high-speed RF interconnect), and the substrate or interposer that ties them together, glass, silicon, ceramic or organic. Few people have worked on all of these in equal depth, and we don't expect you to have. We do expect you to understand how a choice in one area constrains the others, and to be able to reason through the trade-offs with us.

Alongside the builds, you'll advance our packaging methods from bench-level assembly toward repeatable, pilot-production-ready processes, characterise what you build yourself and use the results to debug and refine, and bring packaging constraints upstream into design reviews so that packageability and yield are designed in rather than fixed later. You'll also help establish engineering and characterisation processes that suit a small, fast-moving team today and still hold up as we grow.

• 
Experience: 5+ years in photonics engineering with deep, hands-on expertise in advanced PIC packaging. Demonstrated ownership of at least one packaging technology from lab prototype toward pilot production is highly preferred.

• 
Technical Background: A strong engineering or scientific background in photonics, integrated optics or a related field, with genuine hands-on advanced PIC packaging experience. You should have a working understanding of the breadth of modern packaging, optical coupling and attach, high-speed RF and DC electrical interfaces, and interposer and substrate technologies, even where your own depth sits in one or two of them. Working knowledge of optical characterisation methods and instrumentation, and comfort interpreting the data yourself, is essential.

• 
Education: A master's or Ph.D. in Photonics, Optical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related field.

• 
Nice to have: Photonic design or modelling experience, comfort running simulations to inform packaging trade-offs, reliability qualification experience, or experience working with external foundry, substrate or assembly partners.

• 
Collaboration & Communication: You are a clear communicator who can engage both engineering peers and leadership on technical trade-offs. You are comfortable operating with autonomy and thrive in a small, collaborative, fast-paced deep-tech environment.

The Perks

jobs.description:
The Department of Psychology, Faculty of Social Sciences, University of Copenhagen (UCPH), invites applications for a fully funded 3-year PhD-position from 1 May 2027 or after agreement.  
 
 The position and the project
 The successful candidate will work on the project Treatments for Complex PTSD (RECONNECT-trial), a randomized controlled trial conducted in the Mental Health Services. The project has a strong focus on patient involvement and investigating mechanisms of change within the three intervention arms (Prolonged Exposure, Eye Movement Desensitization Reprocessing and Enhanced Emotional and Interpersonal Skills Training). The project is conducted in collaboration between researchers in psychology and psychiatry.
 
 Duties and responsibilities
 The PhD student will be central in the research project, being involved in and responsible for large parts of the data collection. Most importantly, the PhD-student will be responsible for conceptualizing and conducting a subset of studies. As such, data management and data analyses, as well as manuscript preparation and communication of research results to the scientific community as well as to relevant stakeholders will be central.

  The PhD-student will be responsible for the assessment of the participants with the International Trauma Interview in Danish, overseeing recruitment progress, and conducting quantitative and qualitative research based on survey and interview data. Experience with quantitative and qualitative data analysis is a must. The candidate must have strong clinical skills and preferably with trauma populations. The candidate must be able to work independently under supervision. Collaborative skills and team spirit are in high regard. For the right candidate, there will be ample possibilities to influence the project and develop new project ideas within the project frame.
 
 Supervision and research group
 The PhD-student will be part of a research group at the Department of Psychology conducting psychological and psychiatric research on psychotherapy and trauma.
 
 Qualification requirements
 Applicants must have qualifications corresponding to master’s level related to the subject area of the project, e.g. Psychology. If you have completed your education in Denmark, you must have a master’s degree covered by the collective agreement for academics in the state sector.

  If you have completed your education outside of Denmark, you must either have a master’s degree equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (two years) or as minimum a bachelor’s degree equivalent to a Danish bachelor’s degree (three years) and be assessed as having professional qualifications at master's level.

  If you have completed your education outside of Denmark, we may obtain an assessment of your education from the Danish Research Agency.
 
 Place of employment
 The Department of Psychology, Faculty of Social Sciences, University of Copenhagen (https://psychology.ku.dk/) is a vibrant, inclusive workplace hosting a large group of faculty, post docs and PhD-students. The research of the department covers a wide range of topics and methodologies and has an international work environment.

  Strategy of the Faculty of the Social Sciences
 The Department of Psychology is part of the Faculty of the Social Sciences. The faculty is a successful academic community that strives to put knowledge into action by:

   	
• Engaging partners in the co-creation of knowledge, learning and social change. 	
• Empowering our students to become reflective and responsible citizens who have the vision, the knowledge and the competence to change society for the better. 	
• Energizing global, European and Danish communities of knowledge by innovating research methodologies and by research findings with impact   For more on the faculty strategy, see: https://socialsciences.ku.dk/.
 
 The recruitment process
 Further information on the recruitment process at University of Copenhagen can be found here:  https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/
 
 An Equal Opportunity Workplace
 The University of Copenhagen is committed in its pursuit of academic excellence to equality of opportunity and to creating an inclusive working environment and therefore encourages all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of personal background, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, ethnicity etc. For more on the diverse working place environment at the University and the University’s participation in the HRS4R HR Excellence in Research, see https://employment.ku.dk/working-at-ucph/eu-charter-for-researchers/
 
 International applicant?
 The University of Copenhagen offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including support before and during your relocation and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information about these services as well as information on entering and working in Denmark here: https://ism.ku.dk/
 
 Contact information
 We encourage you to first consult our website, where most questions concerning the recruitment process as well as the academic content and structure of the PhD programme are answered:

  Structure of the PhD programme

  How to obtain a PhD scholarship.

  For information about the project and the position, please contact PI Assistant Professor Sara Kerstine Kaya Nielsen, sara.nielsen@psy.ku.dk. Information about the recruitment process is available from HR, e-mail: HR-SOENDRE@adm.ku.dk Please refer to ID number: 211-2569/26-2H
 
 How to apply
 Submit a complete application at our online portal. Click on the “Apply now” icon at the bottom of the page to apply. The documents must be in Adobe PDF or Word.  

  Your application must be written in English and include the following documents:

   	
• Motivated application 	
• Curriculum vitae 	
• Diploma (master and bachelor) 	
• Other relevant material   
 The deadline for applications is 1 December 2026.
 Applications or enclosures received thereafter will not be considered.
